observations.title: The GPU development self-test ran outside a signed validation window (process deviation)
observations.detail: logs/s3-targeted-native.log records a 41.77 s GPU run (2 passed) on the local RTX 4070 Ti SUPER with CUDA 12.8.1 NVRTC, against an unfrozen target with no window guard, baselines or frozen executables. Under the team GPU-window discipline this is GPU work outside a signed window. The handling is compliant in the record: README §9.3, receipt.s3.dev_self_test.note and the window task note all label it a local development self-test (not a validation window), receipt.s3.window.opened=false and boundaries.window_passed_claimed=false, and no window conclusion is drawn; the window must re-run frozen executables after sign-off.
observations.proposed_action: Register this self-test in the window material/ledger (time, GPU, command, purpose, duration) and state that future dev self-tests also need a pre-report for out-of-window GPU use.
observations.impact: process only; the numbers are not used as window evidence and no conclusion depends on them

observations.title: 'unit tests are pure CPU, no GPU' is imprecise in a CUDA-ready environment
observations.detail: README §9.1 calls the unit tests pure CPU / no GPU. production_availability_follows_cached_narrowphase_status (cfg feature=cuda) calls narrowphase_backend_status() -> probe_backend_with_cuda(); when driver+device+NVRTC are available it runs compile_program() (NVRTC PTX compilation, no CUDA context and no kernel launch). On this machine NVRTC is not on PATH, so the probe short-circuits at nvrtc_library_present() and the 9 tests finish in 0.03 s; on a machine with CUDA bin on PATH the default unit gate would do a driver query plus NVRTC compilation.
observations.proposed_action: Reword to 'no CUDA context, no kernel launch, does not depend on device results', or make the consistency test inject the compile status instead of probing
observations.impact: claim precision and gate cost only

observations.title: Machine-readable JSON line-count exceptions are not recorded

observations.title: Three-state doc and code disagree about 'probe passed but program missing'
observations.detail: README §9.1 puts 'probe passed but the program cannot be obtained' in state ② (device/program unavailable), but the code and the unit test return DeviceFailure (state ③); the test file header comment also lists it under ② while asserting DeviceFailure.
observations.proposed_action: Classify it explicitly as ③, or reword ② as 'probe-stage failure'
observations.impact: diagnostics wording only; behaviour is safe

observations.title: The nworld rejection test has no executor-zero-call assertion
observations.detail: rejects_non_single_world_before_device_work goes through the production entry and has no injection point, so it cannot count executor calls; the zero-call assertions live in the injected ①/② fallback tests. 'Before any device probe' is guaranteed by code order (prepare_inputs is the first step of run_product_collision), not by that test's assertions.
observations.proposed_action: If the record says the unit test asserts zero executor calls, limit that wording to the injected fallback cases

observations.title: The end-to-end target is not compiled by the default gate
observations.detail: tests/g10_p5_product_collision_wiring_cuda.rs has #![cfg(all(feature = cuda, feature = native-model-probe))]; the default gate (default features, no native-model-probe) does not compile it. This slice covers it with the targeted self-test and the window.
observations.proposed_action: Register 'clippy + compile e2e with native-model-probe' as a targeted gate item
observations.impact: future changes to the e2e target have no automatic protection outside the window
